remaining_gaps: EO 14039 (Aug. 20, 2021): blocked, not submitted. The order's operative commands depend on the Protecting Europe's Energy Security Act of 2019 (PEESA, Pub. L. 116-92 div. F title LXXV, as amended by Pub. L. 116-283 sec. 1242): section 1(a) blocks only persons identified in a report to Congress under PEESA section 7503(a)(1)(B), and section 2 implements PEESA section 7503(b). The held text of 22 U.S.C. 9526 and its note (packet evidence id SUPPLEMENT:HELD14039_11_9fc160f5e30e, unreviewed held text, citable but not a basis by itself) sets out PEESA section 7503(h): the authority to impose sanctions with respect to a person involved in construction of a pipeline project described in section 7503(a)(1)(A), and any sanctions imposed with respect to that project, terminate on the earlier of a Presidential certification or 5 years after enactment on Dec. 20, 2019, that is no later than Dec. 20, 2024. The held evidence therefore indicates that the statutory sanctions regime the order implements ended no later than 2024-12-20, before the 2026-10-14 cutoff, and no held instrument revokes the order. The EO 14024 emergency continuation of March 24, 2026 (91 FR 15515) is now citable as SUPPLEMENT:HELD14039_10_3465cac4124a, but it continues only the IEEPA emergency and does not say whether any blocking under this order survived the PEESA sunset. Still missing for a lawful claim in either direction: (1) a reviewed source (not merely the unreviewed held text) that settles whether the section 7503(h) termination reaches the persons identified under section 7503(a)(1)(B) that section 1(a) of this order blocks, with any Presidential certification under section 7503(h)(1); (2) a source showing whether, how and when OFAC or the President ended the blocking under EO 14039 section 1 or kept it (no held Federal Register text from 2024 to 2026 and no held OFAC list or delisting record mentions EO 14039); (3) a packet-citable current-law basis (the only current-law record for the order, CURRENT:EO:14039#0, was not read as showing the blocking in force). Under the assignment rule this order is not claimed YES; the ledger change, if any, belongs to a separate owner route.
